name: toggle-group
pattern: Toggle buttons following the WAI-ARIA APG Button Pattern, with roving-tabindex focus
responsibility: Provides single/multiple selection for native buttons, synchronized aria-pressed/data-state, and arrow-key focus navigation. Does not provide form input, appearance, or content.

authorMarkup.root: An HTMLElement with data-controller="toggle-group" and role="group", named through aria-label or aria-labelledby referencing nonempty text.
authorMarkup.item: At least one native <button type="button"> with data-toggle-group-target="item" and a unique nonempty data-toggle-group-value. Names must not change with selection; aria-pressed is synchronized by the controller. Use aria-label, aria-labelledby referencing text, or button text. Image/SVG-only buttons require aria-label or aria-labelledby. Ordinary text names exclude SVG, aria-hidden=true, hidden, display:none, visibility:hidden/collapse, content-visibility:hidden, and script/style subtrees.
authorMarkup.boundaries: Toolbar manages focus without selection; toggle-group manages a button selection set in a group role. It does not replace native radio form submission or exclusive selection. Combining toolbar on the same element and nesting composite widgets are outside scope. Nested same-type controllers operate only on items in their Stimulus scope.

semanticElements: The root accessible name is nonempty.
At least one item is required, each a native button type=button beneath the root.
Item values are nonempty and unique, and item names are nonempty.
selected is a JSON string array parsed through Stimulus Array values. Invalid JSON, non-arrays, or arrays containing nonstrings disable enhancement.
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Violations issue the standard English warning once per connection and disable enhancement. Do not complete static attributes, output state, move focus, emit events, or apply public API changes; preserve committed selection/outputs. Revalidate changes to targets, values, names, disabled, and type within the root, resuming when valid. External-label contents are revalidated at the next operation, API call, or root change.
contractValidation.completion: Supply group only when root role is absent, preserving authored role. Report completion with the standard English warning once per connection.
contractValidation.completionExempt: Write aria-pressed as synchronized selection state and tabindex as an operational attribute without warnings. Do not put aria-orientation on group or invent names. Visible referenced labels exclude hidden descendant text; directly referenced hidden labels include their subtree text. Opacity zero or offscreen positioning alone does not invalidate names.

selected.description: Initial selection is a string array, synchronized to the current committed value afterward. Removing the attribute resets to an empty array. Do not reserve unknown values for later-added targets.
Return selected values in DOM order. Assignment removes unknowns/duplicates and normalizes single mode to the first DOM-order value. JS may select disabled items. Do not move focus or emit events.

toggle-group:beforechange.detail: ToggleGroupChangeDetail { selected: string[], previousSelected: string[], reason: 'pointer' | 'keyboard' }, before trusted-click changes. preventDefault cancels the change.

toggle-group:change.detail: ToggleGroupChangeDetail after user-originated commitment. Do not emit for programmatic changes, attribute synchronization, or target changes.

api.selection: Reactivating a selected button deselects it in either mode. Single mode clears other items; multiple mode toggles only the item. Switching to single retains the first selected DOM-order item. Target removal drops its value; disabled changes preserve selection. Do nothing if native click is already defaultPrevented.
api.reentrancy: If beforechange listeners change the API, configuration, or targets, preserve their committed result and discard the original operation. Mutating detail arrays does not affect internal selection. API changes remain committed even if the listener also cancels. Unrelated log additions or focus movement alone do not abort. Root removal or removing its controller attribute counts as disconnection.

keyboard.Tab: One enabled item has tabindex=0; others have -1. Prefer the last genuinely focused enabled item, then an enabled selected item, then the first enabled item.
keyboard.ArrowLeft: Horizontal: focus previous in LTR or next in RTL, wrapping at boundaries.
keyboard.ArrowRight: Horizontal: focus next in LTR or previous in RTL, wrapping at boundaries.
keyboard.ArrowUp: Focus previous in vertical mode; ignore in horizontal mode.
keyboard.ArrowDown: Focus next in vertical mode; ignore in horizontal mode.
keyboard.Enter: Toggle selection through trusted native button click.
keyboard.Space: Toggle selection through trusted native button click.
keyboard.navigation: Arrows/Home/End preserve selection. Exclude native :disabled items, including disabled fieldsets. Ignore modified navigation, IME keydown, and synthetic keydown. Use root computed direction; leave Tab to native behavior.

managedMarkup.root: Complete missing role only; do not output root data-state.
managedMarkup.item: Synchronize aria-pressed=true/false, data-state=on/off, and tabindex=0/-1. Preserve authored IDs and static attributes.

stateOutputs.root: Output state per item, not aggregated on the root. No CSS custom properties.

lifecycle: Register listeners/observers on connect and remove them on disconnect. Queued synchronization must not run while disconnected.
Handle item changes with itemTargetConnected/Disconnected, leaving written state attributes on removed items.
Preserve selection across reconnection without duplicate subscriptions. Public API changes do nothing while disconnected; leave attributes intact.
Asynchronous target/disabled changes correct the Tab stop without moving actual focus.
Track disabled changes on ancestor fieldsets outside the root. Pre-connect target callbacks do not subscribe; synchronize current targets after connect.

observations.item: Group names, pressed state, and navigation announcements
observations.impact: Native buttons and aria-pressed define the public semantics independently of compatibility wording.

acceptanceCriteria: Controller behavior must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Consumers own meaningful names, colors, contrast, and focus indicators.
AAA 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception): selection/deselection available by pointer is also available through Enter/Space.
AAA 3.2.5 Change on Request: move focus only for user keyboard operations, never timers or synchronization.
Verify single/multiple mode, RTL/vertical, cancellation, synthetic events, disabled state, dynamic changes, reconnection, and nesting in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.

Observation, unverified: real-device screen reader compatibility for group names, pressed state, and navigation announcements in the catalog. Public semantics use native buttons and aria-pressed and do not depend on these observations.

testMatrix.description: Initial selection, aria-pressed, data-state, no root aggregate, and authored-attribute preservation
Single/multiple selected getter/setter, normalization, attribute synchronization, and no events
Trusted pointer/Enter/Space selection and deselection, reasons, and event order
Arrows, Home/End, wrapping, Tab stop, vertical/RTL, and preserved selection
Rejecting modifiers, IME, and synthetic keydown
Disabled exclusion including ancestor fieldsets, selection preservation, and all-disabled state
Invalid targets/values/configuration and repair, invalid-JSON warnings, and preservation of existing outputs
Root/item names, external labels, and separate completion/disabling warnings
Target addition/removal/movement and value/configuration/name changes without focus movement
API/configuration/target/disconnect changes in beforechange and detail-array independence
Disconnect listener/observer cleanup, cancellation of queued synchronization, and reconnection
Same-type controller scope and event bubbling isolation
